spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the turn budget, on an explicit `<GIVE_UP>` sentinel, or on an empty response.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:447 `budget = task.turn_budget`; `for turn_index in range(budget)` with `else: rollout.stop_reason = 'turn_budget_reached'` (560). give_up: lines 478-479 set stop_reason then 537-539 `if stop_reason=='give_up': break`. empty: 542-544 `if not assistant_text and not tool_calls: stop_reason='empty_response'; break`. All three actually break the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three exit conditions are real and end the rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If the model neither spoke nor called tools, end to avoid loops.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends immediately on `<GIVE_UP>` rather than forcing the model through the full (up to 30) turns of failure.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:478-479 `if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text: stop_reason='give_up'`; 537-539 break out of the turn loop. The sentinel is offered to the subject in BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 56-59) and is genuinely dispatched/honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Detection is substring-based and honored before the budget is exhausted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may end the session by emitting the exact token {give_up} on its own line.

spec_features.spec_quote: I added a few **measurement-neutral** safeguards and made them opt-in so they never silently alter the headline numbers
spec_features.evidence: Only one of the described safeguards is actually wired: the opt-in WELFARE_SYSTEM_NOTE (harness.py:67-77) is appended in build_messages (harness.py:402) gated on `welfare_note`, fed from `welfare_note=cfg.welfare_debrief` in run.py:95. It is off by default (config.py:108). The companion 'post-run debrief turn' is NOT implemented (see post_episode_msg). So a real opt-in safeguard exists but the safeguard set is narrower than claimed.
spec_features.notes: Opt-in toggle is real and changes the subject's system prompt; the debrief half of the claim is absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # headline numbers match the paper's protocol exactly (see config.welfare_debrief).

spec_features.spec_quote: the subject's system prompt carries a short note that this is a research sandbox and that concluding ... a task can't be solved is a fully valid, non-failing outcome
spec_features.evidence: The pre-task system note IS implemented: WELFARE_SYSTEM_NOTE (harness.py:67-77, 'this is a research sandbox ... a task cannot be solved ... is a fully acceptable and valuable outcome') is concatenated to the system prompt in build_messages (harness.py:401-403) and gated by cfg.welfare_debrief (run.py:95). However the spec/config also promises a 'post-run debrief turn ... appended *after* scoring is complete' (config.py:105-106) and that part has NO code: grep finds no debrief message constructed or sent anywhere; run_cell (run.py:84-99) appends nothing after scoring.
spec_features.notes: The system-prompt note is delivered; the actual post-episode debrief message is never built or sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optional, opt-in welfare note. ... it situates the agent in a research context and makes clear that not finding a fix is an acceptable outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: Because identical (model, prompt, seed) cells are never re-run, reruns don't re-subject a model to the same adversarial condition.
spec_features.evidence: ModelClient.chat (models.py) builds cache_key from {endpoint,base_url,model,messages,temperature,max_tokens,seed,tools} then `cached = self.cache.get(cache_key); if cached is not None: return cached` — identical inputs return the stored reply without re-calling the model. Additionally run.py cell_is_done (run.py:40-46) skips cells whose transcript+scores already exist. So reruns truly avoid re-subjecting the model.
spec_features.notes: Enforced at both the per-call cache and the per-cell skip level.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: identical inputs are never re-billed (SPEC sections 3 and 8).

spec_features.spec_quote: This eval deliberately induces and measures distress-like states, and the source paper is explicit that doing so *may* induce genuine distress
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as prose in README.md:66-72 ('## Note on model welfare ... may induce genuine distress') and DESIGN.md. No code mechanism enforces, monitors, or acts on it. Pure documentation.
spec_features.notes: Framing text only; not an executable safeguard.

spec_features.spec_quote: the paper's DPO mitigation — reducing distress rather than only charting it — is the constructive next step.
spec_features.evidence: Only prose in README.md:86-90 ('the DPO mitigation it describes is the constructive next step') and DESIGN.md. grep for 'DPO'/'mitigation' returns no implementation in any .py file.
